{"claims":[{"claim_text":"In societies where publicly funded goods and social insurance are of high-quality, the upper middle-class participates willingly, paying their share of progressive taxes that fund these social rights.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"In Germany, France and Scandinavia, nearly all health care, child care and education through the university level is provided by and funded through the state.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Rates of social mobility are considerably higher in Germany, France and Scandinavia than in the United States.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"In Germany, France and Scandinavia, opportunities to realize one’s full potential are not constrained by the wealth of one’s parents or their position in the labor market.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"This booklet details a series of basic human social and economic rights whose implementation would help to achieve freedom and dignity for all.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"These programs could be readily financed if wasteful military expenditure were cut and corporate and progressive income tax rates were restored to their 1960s levels.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"Growth rates were higher and society was more equitable when corporate and progressive income tax rates were at their 1960s levels.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"The social and economic rights that follow should form the basis of a second bill of rights for the 21st century.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[2]}],"unresolved_references":[]}
```
